rows.title: What’s Working: Why Colorado Gives Day lasts 39 days. And it starts today.
rows.standfirst: With SNAP benefits temporarily funded, federal worker furloughs and continued rising costs, it’ll be a challenge to top last year’s $54.8 million. Plus: Food Bank of the Rockies already seeing 20% increase in demand for food

rows.title: “Love is Blind” put a spotlight on Colorado. But it’s not the easiest state for filmmakers.
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s filmmakers, producers and crews say there are still significant challenges to making movies in the state

rows.title: Colorado job hunters are using AI. So are employers, scammers and even the state’s labor department.
rows.standfirst: The job market in Colorado and around the country is pitting AI generators against AI filters and leaving real workers and hiring managers feeling trapped in the middle.

rows.title: UCHealth will directly receive taxpayer dollars in Estes Park merger
rows.standfirst: The health system will take over Estes Park Health and receive tax revenue via the Park Hospital District

rows.title: Littleton Ballot Question 3A: Voters approve new restrictions on homebuilding
rows.standfirst: The Littleton city charter amendment will enshrine single-family zoning in the city’s charter and stymie local efforts to add density. Elsewhere, voters in Louisville defeated measures to make it harder to build housing.

rows.title: Vail voters reject new tax on short-term rentals to pay for affordable housing
rows.standfirst: Eagle County on Nov. 17 announced a final count on the ballot measure, with a margin of 35 votes rejecting the 6% tax on short-term rentals.

rows.title: How much business did Tesla lose in Colorado from Elon Musk’s hard right turn?
rows.standfirst: A lot, Yale researchers say, in Colorado and across the country, perhaps more than 1 million car sales

rows.title: Airlines at Denver airport say most flights will remain intact, even as FAA demands 10% reduction in air traffic
rows.standfirst: United Airlines canceled 4% of flights through the weekend. That’s about 20 flights out of Denver International Airport. Many airlines are offering refunds to eligible travelers.

rows.title: Are care workers among the lowest-paid workers in the country?
rows.standfirst: Yes. Care workers earn significantly less than the median U.S. income and consistently rank near the bottom of occupational pay lists.

rows.title: Is AI blowing up our electricity prices? An expert weighs in.
rows.standfirst: Colorado and other states are seeing massive data center growth, and big buyers may squeeze out consumers

rows.title: Federal judge pauses Colorado law requiring social media warnings for younger users
rows.standfirst: Under a law passed last year, companies must program warnings to pop up every 30 minutes once a minor user has spent an hour or more on a platform in a 24-hour period, or between the hours of 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.

rows.title: What’s Working: Even in this economy, the show must go on in Colorado
rows.standfirst: Inflation pushed Colorado theater and arts organizations to offer more affordable options. Plus: Fresca Foods gets Spanish owner, Entegris opens chip plant and wage theft at a record high

rows.title: A Colorado doctor wanted the facts on wolf reintroduction. So he created a watchdog group on Facebook.
rows.standfirst: John Michael Williams thinks Colorado is withholding information on reintroduced wolves from citizens. In changing that, did he create an extremist group?

rows.title: New companies are sprouting up in rural Colorado to benefit local economies
rows.standfirst: Nearly 75 small Colorado businesses in 20 economically challenged counties have benefited from the Rural Jump-Start Program, a state tax incentive created in 2015 via legislation.

rows.title: With one coal-fired plant out for months, Xcel appeals to keep Comanche 2 open beyond December shutdown deadline
rows.standfirst: Plan to meet growing electricity demand is backed by an unlikely band, including the state consumer advocate and energy office. Green groups are not happy.

rows.title: Supreme Court extends its order blocking full SNAP payments, with shutdown potentially near an end
rows.standfirst: In Colorado, the state last week sent full November SNAP payments to 32,000 people before the Supreme Court halted the distributions

rows.title: On Colorado’s Western Slope, many farmworkers are afraid like never before
rows.standfirst: Western Slope farmers have been in tense survival mode since the Trump administration first promised to apprehend and deport undocumented immigrants.

rows.title: US Mint presses final pennies as production ends after more than 230 years
rows.standfirst: Over the last century, about half of the coins made at mints in Philadelphia and Denver have been pennies

rows.title: Are the Broncos set to demolish the Denver Water offices for a new stadium?
rows.standfirst: No. The Broncos have no plans to demolish Denver Water’s administrative building to make room for a new stadium at the Burnham Yards.

rows.title: Tri-State expects federal order to keep coal-fired power plant in northwestern Colorado running
rows.standfirst: The first of the generating station’s three units, and the coal mine that supplies it, was to close in December

rows.title: What’s Working: Why Finland’s ambassador was checking out Colorado’s quantum industry
rows.standfirst: She wasn’t the only international guest. The local quantum computing Tech Hub has also been meeting with folks from the UK and Australia.

rows.title: Are rent prices in Denver actually falling? Here’s a look behind the industry data.
rows.standfirst: With free months and other concessions, Denver’s rents may be falling faster than the industry data shows. But not everyone is seeing lower rents.

rows.title: “Even worse than we thought”: Colorado is stuck in a cycle of annual, $1B state budget shortfalls
rows.standfirst: Each year the cycle continues, state lawmakers will have fewer ways to address the gap without cutting state programs and services. Skyrocketing Medicaid costs are primarily to blame.

rows.title: United Power seeks “hyperlocal” energy for Colorado customers after dumping longtime supplier
rows.standfirst: The Brighton-based co-op is building a portfolio of suppliers after paying $627M in 2024 to exit Tri-State Generation and Transmission Association contract

rows.title: Vail voters reject plan to tax short-term rentals to support housing
rows.standfirst: The Vail Town Council hoped to raise more than $7 million a year for workforce housing with a 6% excise tax on Vail’s 2,600 short-term rental homes

rows.title: Why are more people becoming preppers? Colorado survivalists say natural disasters, COVID and doomsday.
rows.standfirst: Spurred partly by natural disasters such as wildfires and the COVID-19 pandemic, more people are taking stock of their ability to survive a few days on their own.

rows.title: The non-DOGE effort to suss out underused federal properties toured Denver Federal Center this week
rows.standfirst: The director of an independent board created during the Obama administration visited the Lakewood federal workforce campus as part of a data-gathering mission

rows.title: What’s Working: Thanksgiving dinner in Colorado will cost less than last year, as grocers eat the loss
rows.standfirst: And turkeys are still available! Plus: Items that cost more or less, Thanksgiving travel, AMP and the nation’s largest recycling center, a downtown office-to-apartment conversion, more!

rows.title: US patent agency asks where to put new regional office after closing its Denver hub
rows.standfirst: A month after shutting down the regional office in Denver, the patent agency is seeking locations for a new one. The deadline is 3 p.m. Friday

rows.title: Xcel Energy asks for $356M rate increase that will boost Colorado residential customers’ bills by about $10
rows.standfirst: The company acknowledged affordability problems and proposed doubling the energy assistance fee 1.6 million customers pay monthly

rows.title: Colorado unveils effort to help affordable housing developers navigate mountain of paperwork for tax credits, financing
rows.standfirst: The Housing Hub Colorado is a one-stop website offering developers information on housing tax credits and financing options and how to apply. It will be followed by a common application.

rows.title: Holiday food boxes make a kindly connection between Colorado farms and families
rows.standfirst: Aid organizations say sourcing ingredients from local farmers, ranchers and greenhouses gives growers an end-of-season boost while helping others

rows.title: International tourists will pay $100 more to enter Rocky Mountain National Park, can’t visit on fee-free days
rows.standfirst: “America-first entry fee policies” announced by the National Park Service apply to the 11 most popular parks and include increasing the price foreign travelers pay for an annual pass to $250

rows.title: 14 US stadiums, including Denver’s Mile High, proposed among 20 possible sites for 2031 Women’s World Cup
rows.standfirst: Organizers envision fan festivals and watch parties in conjunction with games. Revenue from marketing and sponsorships is projected at $1.4 billion.
